**Simple Drive parabolic antenna  
used in RadioSkyMap**


RadioSkyMap is able to control your telescope mount with the ASCOM universal telescope interface.   
But for larger antennas or for those who do not have a control system for their antenna, it is possible to make a simple and low-cost system to control the pointing of your antenna at least in height. This system described below is implemented in RadioSkyMap and allows automatic pointing and observation in "Meridian Transit" mode or to make "drift scan" of the radio sky that can be used by the ezRA software for example.

The easiest solution.  
DC power supply with dual switch, using schematic below :

Other solutions with dedicated electronic components exist. But in my opinion, this one is the simplest, the most economical and the most reliable in the long term.   
  


4. USB relay used and implemented in RadioSkyMap  
  
RadioSkyMap drive directly 2 to 8 relay through USB relay interface.  
This interface is very common, inexpensive and can be easily found on Amazon or Aliexpress.  
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Simply connect it via a USB cable to your computer and RadioSkyMap will drive the actuator's motor.

6. Antenna position control (Only in height) for meridian transit observations. 

In order to simplify as much as possible the electronic realization of the antenna position control (at least in height), we will use an Arduino that directly integrates IMU-type position sensors. It is the Arduino nano 33 Ble.   
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)  
  
So no soldering or complicated wiring, you just have to position the Arduino module correctly on the antenna and connect it by a USB cable to the computer that runs RadioSkyMap (as for the USB relay board) .  
The electronic board is flat when the antenna is horizontal and normally when the antenna rises there is a change in the value of the IMU which measures the x position as the antenna rises. The code (sketch for Arduino IDE) below will transmit the x-position angle in degrees to RadioSkyMap on the USB port, which will be able to control the actuator motor to go to a position assigned in the software.



7. Arduino nano 33 Ble sketch to measure height angle (0.1° precision)  
  
**/\*  
  Arduino BMI270\_BMM150 - Accelerometer Application**

  **This example reads the acceleration values as relative direction and degrees,**

  **from the BMI270 sensor and prints them to the Serial Monitor.**

  **The circuit:**

  **- Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2**

  **Created by Pedro Lima**

  **This example code is in the public domain.**

**\*/**


**\#include "Arduino\_BMI270\_BMM150.h"**


**\#define MINIMUM\_TILT 0    // Threshold for tilt detection in degrees**

**\#define WAIT\_TIME 150     // How often to run the code (in milliseconds)**


**float x, y, z;**

**float angleX = 0;**

**int angleY = 0;**

**unsigned long previousMillis = 10;**


**void setup() \{**


  **Serial.begin(9600);**

  **while (!Serial);**


  **if (!IMU.begin()) \{**

    **Serial.println("Failed to initialize IMU!");**

    **while (1);**

  **\}**


  **Serial.print("Accelerometer sample rate = ");**

  **Serial.print(IMU.accelerationSampleRate());**

  **Serial.println("Hz");**

**\}**


**void loop() \{**

  **if (IMU.accelerationAvailable() && millis() - previousMillis \>= WAIT\_TIME) \{**

    **previousMillis = millis();**

    **IMU.readAcceleration(x, y, z);**


    **// Calculate tilt angles in degrees**

    **angleX = atan2(x, sqrt(y \* y + z \* z)) \* 180 / PI;**

    **angleY = atan2(y, sqrt(x \* x + z \* z)) \* 180 / PI;**

    **Serial.println(angleX);   **

    


  **\}**

**\}**


That all for drive your antenna in height.

  
For Azimut drive the encoder is necessary.   
It is not implemented in RadioSkyMap at this time, because I whant to find inexpensive solution an a simple solution to implement by someone who is not necessarily an electronics engineer.
